newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Fourth letter bomb suspected at United Nations.
newsitem.headline: Fourth letter bomb suspected at United Nations.

text.p: A fourth suspected letter bomb was found at the United Nations early on Tuesday, security sources said.

The sources, who asked not to be identified, said New York police were determining whether the supicious letter was similar to three other explosive devices found on Monday morning and evening and addressed to an Arab-language newspaper.
"It looks like all the others, " said one source.

The three previous letter bombs discovered on Monday were addressed to the U.N. bureau of the Arabic-language newspaper Al-Hayat. U.N. personnel intend to search tens of thousands of pieces of mail throughout the night.

The letters at the United Nations were similar to those mailed earlier this month to the newspaper's Washington bureau. U.N. sources said the letters, like those received in Washington, bore an Alexandria, Egypt, postmark.

Before the letter bombs were discovered at the United Nations on Monday, a bomb exploded at the London headquarters of Al-Hayat, wounding two security guards. Four more suspected devices were subsequently found there, British police said.
